items.text: fixed: in Edit with Halo off, the colour and mark bar no longer pushes the bottom bar off the screen and makes the page scroll. The stage now makes room for the bar when it appears (and takes the room back when it goes), counting its margins and gap.

changed: switching Halo on and off in Edit now morphs: the colour and mark bar slides up and grows its room (and slides down and gives it back), instead of snapping. The pencil's other changes (Performance, view, MIDI leaving the right rail) slide the same way.
changed: in Edit, the heads-up display button stays at the bottom of the right rail, where it is in play, so it is where your hand looks for it.

changed: in Edit, on an iPad or desktop the colours and the eight mark types now sit together on one compact centred line (smaller, close-set buttons) instead of spreading across the whole width. Phones keep the two-row layout.

changed: the Guide now says what the robot does. It opens with the goal (playing as a shared responsibility, handed from the app to the player to an ensemble, on any device, for every age, group and ability), then names three ways to play (by the robot, by hand, by the field), explains the robot and its Automation helpers, and the play lines and line-ups it plays.

changed: in the Index, a word in a paragraph that names a control shown in the same section (Air, Texture, Space, Morph, Session name, Line-up, Open the report) is now bold and in the strong ink, with the control's own icon when it has one. It is worked out from the controls themselves, so it follows them if they change.

fixed: the heads-up display's footer band now runs edge to edge and down to the pop-up's lower edge: its tab buttons fill the band's full height, with no wasted strip beneath. The yellow mark above the open tab is a straight line sitting right on the border between the band and the pane above, with no rounded ends, as in the side menus.

added: a Settings section in the Index, as in Current. Words: Always, Learn (the default: a control's word shows at first, then fades once you have used it about five times, and comes back when you press it) or Never (icons only; screen readers still hear every word). Theme: Auto, Light or Dark. Both are kept on this device.

changed: a scene is now a score, everywhere you read it: the bar's previous and next score, the dice ("roll a new score"), the status line ("Score 1 of 1"), the Scores tab and pane, the index and the guide. A score is the musical state: the grid, the lines, the tempo and the feel. "Scene" is kept for a future visual layer. The export that was called "score" is now called "notation" so the word means one thing.
